signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Workbook median is 2.94 g/t — sitting at the Strong/Moderate boundary. P95 is 43.5 g/t. Deposit-type adjustments still apply (porphyry vs orogenic vs vein).

signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Workbook does not separately tag UG vs OP — both styles sit in the same gold dataset. UG-style high-grade narrow intercepts are dominant in the high-grade flagged rows (60% of the 9,764).

exceptional.label: Perpendicular to vein/structure + true width reported

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Catches the 'director's hole' trick: drilling along a thin gold sheet inflates apparent width. Perpendicular holes give true thickness.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: ⚠ NOT IN WORKBOOK SCHEMA. Azimuth, dip, and true width fields are not extracted by the pipeline. Available fields: hole_id, intercept_length_m, from_depth_m, to_depth_m only. Requires pipeline expansion or curator-led extraction from original filings.

weak.label: Step-out drilling, target testing, new zone — predominantly exploration

signals.name: Interval Width (m)
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Width drives tonnage potential and mining method. Wide intercepts → open-pit; narrow → selective UG. Per Reuben's request: width as its own scoring axis.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Deposit-type dependent — 5m is narrow for a porphyry, normal for a vein. Cross-check with Deposit-Type Adjustments. Width alone insufficient — pair with grade.

sourceLinks.label: Workbook empirical distribution by commodity
See Empirical Calibration sheet for percentiles

workbookAnchors: Top widths: PAAS 1,600m, Copper Giant 693m, American Eagle 618m, NGEx 335m.

signals.name: Grade × Width (GT Product)
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Per Reuben: 'quality matrix like quality to grade into width.' GT product is a single normalized metric capturing both high-grade-narrow and low-grade-bulk on the same scale. Tiers are PURE empirical breakpoints — top 5/25/50/75% of each commodity's workbook distribution.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: GT alone can't distinguish 1m @ 100 g/t from 100m @ 1 g/t — both are GT=100. Use GT alongside separate grade and width signals. Apply deposit-type adjustments.

Per-commodity percentile breakpoints

resources.name: Resource Estimates
resources.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Thresholds sourced from CIM Definition Standards (NI 43-101), industry convention on M&I splits, and 'world class' benchmarks. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual resource statements. To validate: build a database of NI 43-101 technical reports with tonnage/grade/classification splits across a representative set of projects and compute real percentile breakpoints.

signals.name: Resource Confidence (Category Mix)

redFlag.label: No formal resource / Historical estimate only

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: M&I can underpin PFS/DFS and convert to reserves. Inferred cannot be included in PFS/DFS economics.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Per NI 43-101: Inferred resources are too speculative for mine planning. JORC is slightly more permissive. A maiden resource that is mostly Inferred still has value as a first step.

sourceLinks.label: CIM Definition Standards (NI 43-101 resource categories)
Wikipedia — NI 43-101 overview (M&I vs Inferred)

signals.name: Tonnage Change vs Prior MRE
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Tonnage growth shows the deposit is getting bigger. >15% is "significant" per market convention.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Tonnage can grow by lowering cut-off grade (adds tonnes but dilutes grade). Always check if grade held or improved alongside tonnage growth.

sourceLinks.label: Proactive Investors — Mining 101: Resources, Reserves, JORC & NI 43-101
Brunswick Exploration — Maiden MRE example (52.2 Mt @ 1.08% Li₂O)

signals.name: Grade Change vs Prior MRE
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Grade uplift is rare and highly valued by the market. It means the deposit is richer than previously thought.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Grade changes can be driven by: new high-grade zones included, different cut-off applied, or improved geological model. Always compare like-for-like cut-off grades.

sourceLinks.label: Apollo Silver — Updated MRE example (61% tonnage increase, 14% Ag oz increase)
CIM Definition Standards — Resource classification

signals.name: Contained Metal Scale
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Absolute contained metal determines whether the deposit justifies the capex to build a mine.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: 'World class' thresholds vary: Singer defines world-class gold at ≥3.2 Moz, copper at ≥2 Mt, silver at ≥77 Moz. Smaller deposits can still be economic if high-grade and well-located.

sourceLinks.label: INN — World-class gold deposit: ≥3.2 Moz (Singer definition)
INN — World-class silver deposit: ≥77 Moz (Singer definition)

signals.name: Cut-off / Reporting Consistency

exceptional.label: Like-for-like update with transparent cut-off and assumptions

redFlag.label: Opaque reporting / not comparable to prior MRE

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Resource growth or grade change is hard to trust if cut-off, density or metal price assumptions shift materially.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Always compare the old and new cut-off grade, density assumptions and metal prices before interpreting resource growth.

metallurgy.name: Metallurgical Results
metallurgy.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Recovery thresholds from 911 Metallurgist, AusIMM test scale guidance, and Canada Nickel recovery improvement examples. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual metallurgical test results. To validate: build a database of PEA/PFS/DFS reports with recovery rates, test scales, and ore complexity assessments across multiple commodity types.

signals.name: Primary Recovery Rate
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Recovery directly impacts revenue. Each 1pp of recovery ≈ 1% of project NPV for most deposits.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Sel's point: recovery is highly project-specific. A tertiary crusher took one project from ~45% to >75%. Process route optimization can dramatically shift results.

sourceLinks.label: 911 Metallurgist — Recovery formulas and accounting
Umbrex — Grade quality and metallurgical recovery analysis

signals.name: Recovery Improvement vs Prior Test
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Improvement signals the processing team has found a better route. >10pp is a "met breakthrough."
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Improvement source matters: pilot-scale > bench-scale. Also check if improvement came from changing ore type (oxide vs sulphide) or actual process optimization.

sourceLinks.label: Canada Nickel — Recovery improvement example (46%→52%)
Process Mineralogy Today — Theoretical grade-recovery curve

signals.name: Test Scale & Reliability

moderate.label: Batch flotation or column leach test

weak.label: Bottle roll or simple leach test

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Higher scale = higher confidence that results will replicate at full plant.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Locked-cycle tests are the minimum for PFS economics. Pilot plant results are preferred for DFS. Batch tests are indicative only.

sourceLinks.label: AusIMM — Metallurgical testing methods (bench→pilot→demo)
911 Metallurgist — Common processing calculations

signals.name: Ore Complexity / Penalty Risk

redFlag.label: Refractory + high penalty + no viable process route

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Deleterious elements (As, Sb, F, Mn, Bi) attract smelter penalties or require special processing.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Refractory gold has evolved (HPGR, tertiary crushing, bio-oxidation) per Sel's feedback. "Refractory" is no longer a death sentence but still adds $30–50/t to processing cost.

sourceLinks.label: ScienceDirect — Concentrate grade vs recovery trade-off
Mining.com — Canada Nickel concentrate grades & penalties

signals.name: Variability Coverage by Ore Domain

exceptional.label: Multiple domains tested; variability understood and design basis robust

moderate.label: Key domains tested but gaps remain

weak.label: Single composite or limited samples only

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Metallurgy often fails at scale because one composite sample was treated as representative of the full orebody.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Domains should reflect oxide / transition / fresh, high-Mg zones, clay-rich zones or penalty-element domains where relevant.

economicStudies.name: Economic Studies
economicStudies.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. IRR / NPV / Payback / AISC thresholds from Junior Mining Network, Cassels study accuracy ranges, Deep Value Signals junior mining rules, and Rupert Resources PFS AISC benchmarks. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual feasibility study outputs. To validate: build a database of PEA/PFS/DFS filings with their reported economics and compute real breakpoints.

signals.name: Study Confidence Level
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: DFS = bankable, can underwrite project finance. PFS = directional. PEA = conceptual, includes Inferred resources.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: PEA economics that include Inferred resources are speculative per NI 43-101. The cautionary language is mandatory. A PEA should never be treated as a PFS.

sourceLinks.label: Cassels — NI 43-101: PEA vs PFS vs FS economic analysis
Next Investors — Feasibility studies explained (PEA ±35%, PFS ±25%, DFS ±15%)

signals.name: IRR (Post-Tax)
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: IRR must exceed the hurdle rate for the jurisdiction. Stable jurisdictions: 15%. High-risk: 25–30%.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: IRR is highly sensitive to commodity price assumption. Always check the base case price vs current spot. A "50% IRR" at $3,000/oz gold is less impressive than 25% at $1,800/oz.

sourceLinks.label: Junior Mining Network — PEA/PFS/DFS results with IRR examples
Deep Value Signals — Junior Mining 101 (NPV, IRR, AISC explained)

signals.name: NPV vs Market Cap Ratio
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Shows how much of the project's value the market has priced in. >1× means upside remains.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Compare at base case price, not spot. Also check if NPV includes Inferred resources (PEA) vs M&I only (PFS/DFS).

sourceLinks.label: Deep Value Signals — Junior Mining 101 (EV/NPV discounts)
Rupert Resources PFS — NPV example ($1.7B, IRR 38%)

signals.name: Payback Period
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Shorter payback = faster capital return = lower financing risk.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Payback is a simple (non-discounted) metric. Should be used alongside NPV/IRR, not in isolation.

sourceLinks.label: Next Investors — Feasibility studies: payback explained
First Mining — Springpole PFS: 1.8yr payback example

signals.name: Price Assumption Conservatism

exceptional.label: Base case below or near long-term consensus / spot-adjusted conservative

weak.label: Aggressive pricing required to make study work

redFlag.label: Study only works on stretched price deck

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: A strong study should still look investable under conservative pricing assumptions.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Always compare study assumptions to current spot, consensus and long-term decks. High IRR at unrealistic prices is a red flag.

signals.name: AISC Position on Global Cost Curve
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Lower cost = survives commodity price downturns. Bottom quartile producers rarely shut down.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: AISC definition varies between companies. Always check what's included (sustaining capex, royalties, G&A). Some exclude corporate G&A.

sourceLinks.label: Rupert Resources PFS — AISC $759/oz (lowest quartile example)
Atlantic Lithium Ewoyaa DFS — AISC $610/t SC6

permitting.name: Permitting
permitting.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Permit progress and social licence tiers from Client Earth (Ghana EIA/mining licence framework) and Gordon Foundation IBA Community Tool. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual permit timelines. To validate: build a database of mining project permit histories across the 8 Minestarters jurisdictions with timelines and outcomes.

signals.name: Permit Progress

exceptional.label: All key permits granted (EIA + Mining Licence)

strong.label: EIA approved, Mining Licence in progress

redFlag.label: Permit refused or under legal challenge

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Permits are binary risk events. EIA + Mining Licence together unlock the construction decision.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Timelines are jurisdiction-specific. Ghana EPA: 6–12 months. Canada CEAA: 2–5 years. Australia: varies by state. Don't compare across jurisdictions.

sourceLinks.label: Client Earth — Ghana mining licence/EPA permit process
Atlantic Lithium — Ewoyaa permit milestones (Mining Lease → EPA → Mine Operating Permit)

signals.name: Community & Social Licence

exceptional.label: Broad community support + benefit agreement signed

redFlag.label: Legal injunction or blockade in place

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Social licence can halt a permitted project. IBA (Impact Benefit Agreement) with indigenous groups is critical in Canada/Australia.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Social risk is often underpriced by the market until it causes a delay. A granted permit with community opposition is less valuable than it appears.

sourceLinks.label: Gordon Foundation — IBA Community Toolkit
Cassels — IBAs in mining: role of government

offtake.name: Offtake / Partnerships
offtake.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Offtake strength and partner quality tiers from MiningWorld offtake analysis and PPX Mining / Glencore strategic investment example. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual offtake agreements. To validate: build a database of executed offtake agreements with binding status, pricing mechanism, volume coverage, and counterparty tier classification.

signals.name: Offtake Strength

exceptional.label: Binding LOM offtake with Tier-1 + prepayment

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Binding agreements underwrite project finance. MOUs are non-binding but signal demand.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Binding vs MOU is the critical distinction. An MOU with a Tier-1 is less valuable than a binding deal with a Tier-2.

sourceLinks.label: MiningWorld — Offtake agreements and why they unlock financing
Mining Doc — What are offtake agreements in mining

signals.name: Binding Nature / Commercial Depth

exceptional.label: Binding deal + pricing / take-or-pay / financing linkage

strong.label: Binding offtake with clear commercial terms

moderate.label: Advanced MOU / term sheet with credible counterparty

redFlag.label: Non-binding announcement with no commercial substance

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Markets often overreact to MOUs; true value comes from enforceability and financing relevance.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Look for prepayments, equity, minimum offtake volumes, pricing formula, impurities and termination clauses.

signals.name: Strategic Partner Quality

exceptional.label: Top-5 global player + equity stake at premium

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: A Tier-1 partner (Glencore, Trafigura, Toyota Tsusho, etc.) validates the project to other investors and lenders.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Equity component at a premium is the strongest signal (partner believes in upside). Prepayment is second-best (partner commits capital).

sourceLinks.label: PPX Mining / Glencore — Strategic investment + offtake example
NMG/Panasonic — Binding offtake with Tier-1 example (13,000 tpa)

capitalRaises.name: Capital Raises
capitalRaises.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Financing signal and dilution thresholds from Deep Value Signals junior mining rules. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual capital raises. To validate: build a database of junior mining raises with discount vs market, dilution percentage, and subsequent share price performance.

signals.name: Financing Signal
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: How capital is raised signals market demand for the stock. Premium = strong demand. Deep discount = weak.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Dilution context matters: a 10% dilution that fully funds to production is better than a 3% raise that only covers 6 months of G&A.

sourceLinks.label: Deep Value Signals — Junior Mining 101 (dilution, financing)
Arizona Sonoran Copper PFS — NPV/IRR/Capex metrics

signals.name: Runway to Next Value Milestone

exceptional.label: Fully funded to next major value event + contingency

moderate.label: Funded to interim work program only

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Funding quality matters less if the raise does not actually get the project to a material rerating event.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: A small, low-dilution raise can still be weak if it only funds G&A. Investors care about funded pathway to drill, resource, PEA, permit or construction decision.

signals.name: Dilution Impact
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Dilution erodes existing shareholder value. "Fully funded to next milestone" is the key test.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Calculate on a fully-diluted basis (include warrants, options, convertibles). Published shares outstanding often understates true dilution.

sourceLinks.label: Deep Value Signals — Junior Mining 101 (dilution mechanics)
Crux Investor — Analyst's Notes: drill results interpretation

construction.name: Construction / Production
construction.provenanceNote: PUBLISHED REFERENCE ONLY. Ramp-up performance, grade reconciliation, schedule, and capex overrun thresholds from Snowden Optiro technical due diligence and AMC Consultants DD guidance. NOT empirically calibrated against a dataset of actual mining project construction outcomes. To validate: build a database of recent mine builds with their DFS predictions vs actual performance.

signals.name: Ramp-Up Performance
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Ramp-up speed shows execution capability. Faster = earlier cash flow.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Ramp-up is where most juniors stumble. The "valley of death" between first ore and commercial production is the highest-risk period.

sourceLinks.label: Snowden Optiro — Technical due diligence for mining acquisitions
AMC Consultants — Technical due diligence for mining

signals.name: Grade Reconciliation

exceptional.label: Actual head grade within ±5% of mine plan

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Head grade vs plan shows if the resource estimate was accurate and if mining is following the plan.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Negative grade reconciliation (actual < plan) is the most common problem for new producers. It can cascade into lower production and higher unit costs.

sourceLinks.label: AMC Consultants — Technical DD (reconciliation audits)
Latin Mines — Drill result analysis & grade filtering

signals.name: Schedule vs Plan

exceptional.label: First production on or ahead of plan

signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Schedule slips often precede cost overruns and equity dilution.
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Differentiate first ore, first concentrate, first production and commercial production. The market often rewards first ore, but lenders focus on commercial production.

signals.name: Capex vs Budget
signals.whatDrivesTheBadge: Capex overruns dilute IRR and may require additional financing (= more dilution).
signals.caveatDepositTypeNuance: Overruns are common in mining. Industry average is ~20% over DFS estimate. On-budget delivery is actually exceptional.

sourceLinks.label: AMC Consultants — Are proposed costs reasonable & adequate?
Spanish Mountain PEA — NPV & capex comparison (PFS vs PEA)

drillProgramSubRubric.name: Drill Exploration-vs-Resource Sub-Rubric (58 weighted signals across 9 categories)
drillProgramSubRubric.analystSource: Linked sub-sheet from the 'Drill Program Type' row of the main matrix. Sum all matching signals per release; higher total (exploration vs resource) wins. Per Reuben: 'each drill has to be classified as an exploration drill or a resource drill.'
drillProgramSubRubric.decisionRule: For each release, sum +N exploration weights against +N resource weights across every matching signal in every category. The higher total classifies the release. If both totals are 0, fall through to the Data Quality fallback category.

categories.name: Program Intent (language-based)
categories.strongestSingleCategoryNote: 20 signals in this category — strongest single category in the rubric. Direct language match scores +5 resource or +5 exploration.
categories.caveat: Same release may contain multiple phrases — sum scores across matches, higher total classifies.
workbookExamples: Anfield Energy — 'exploration-phase drilling' → scored 80
Hercules Metals — 'Outlines Initial 2026 Drill Plan at Leviathan' → scored 80
West Red Lake Gold — Rowan Mine 'resource conversion drilling' language at Madsen

categories.name: Resource Linkage
categories.strongestSingleCategoryNote: 7 signals in this category. All bias toward Resource classification — no exploration weights.
categories.caveat: If the release explicitly mentions an MRE (current or upcoming), this category carries decisive weight.
workbookExamples: Orla Mining — sequential Camino Rojo MRE updates
West Red Lake Gold — Madsen + Rowan MRE history (priority vault VLT-004)
Pan American Silver — producer-grade resource statements

categories.name: Geological Context
categories.caveat: Distinguishes drilling that tests geological hypotheses (exploration) from drilling that fills in known geology (resource).
workbookExamples: West Red Lake Gold — 'extends Vein Zones' language at Rowan
Hercules Metals — Leviathan extension at depth
Banyan Gold — AurMac anomaly testing

categories.name: Project Stage
categories.caveat: Project stage alone is not decisive — always combine with program intent and resource linkage signals.
workbookExamples: West Red Lake Gold — Production Restart stage → resource-leaning
Greatland Gold — Production stage → resource
Eloro Resources — PEA stage → mixed with resource lean

categories.name: Drill Spacing (where disclosed)
categories.notInWorkbookSchemaNote: ⚠ NOT DERIVABLE FROM WORKBOOK. The drill validation pipeline does not extract inter-hole spacing. Spacing data must come from NI 43-101 technical reports or curated extraction from press releases.
categories.caveat: Deposit-type dependent: porphyries tolerate wider spacing than narrow vein systems. Cross-check with Deposit-Type Adjustments sheet.

categories.name: Location Context
categories.notInWorkbookSchemaNote: ⚠ NOT DERIVABLE FROM WORKBOOK. No coordinates or geospatial fields. However, document_title often contains proxy phrases like 'extends Vein Zones', 'step-out NE of HER-24-12', 'new high-grade silver veins' that can be NLP-extracted.
categories.caveat: Spatial relationship to known mineralization — hardest category to score automatically.
workbookExamples: West Red Lake Gold — 'extends Vein Zones' [Rowan]
Hercules Metals — '220m step-out NE of HER-24-12' [Leviathan]
Banyan Gold — 'new high-grade silver veins' [AurMac]

categories.name: Release Language (direct quotes)
categories.caveat: Watch for promotional language inflation ('district-scale potential') — weight less than specific resource phrases.
workbookExamples: Brixton Metals — 'Reports Record Silver Intercepts' → exploration language
Marimaca Copper — 'Additional High-Grade Silver Assays' → resource-supporting
Nine Mile Metals — 'Certified Assays' → resource confidence language

categories.name: Campaign Composition
categories.caveat: When campaign composition triggers, classify section by section within the release rather than assigning one label to the whole thing.
workbookExamples: Orla Mining — Camino Rojo programs blend infill + step-out
Hercules Metals — Leviathan combines step-out with extension
New Gold — Rainy River underground + surface rig combined

categories.name: Data Quality (fallback)
categories.caveat: If all 8 other categories score 0/0, classify as Mixed/Unclear. Do not force a classification on insufficient text.
workbookExamples: Many stockhead and jmn aggregator snippets lack enough text for confident classification
Short press release summaries often omit program intent entirely
